title: Desertion as a divorce ground - how long must it actually last
p1: Can a spouse simply leave the marriage and claim divorce after a few months? Many people assume separation alone is enough. The law looks at a deeper question.
p2: A common misconception is that any period of living separately amounts to desertion. In reality, desertion as a ground for divorce generally requires the spouse to have left the other person without a valid reason and without intending to return. Under Indian divorce law, this abandonment must usually continue for a continuous period of two years before filing for divorce.
p3: The surprising part? The clock does not start merely because someone moves out. The circumstances behind the separation matter. A spouse forced to leave due to cruelty or genuine reasons may not be considered the one who deserted the marriage. The law examines intention, conduct, and the reasons for separation. A simple takeaway: physical distance is not always legal desertion.
conclusion: Do you think a fixed two-year period is fair in every desertion case, or should the law allow more flexibility based on circumstances?
